maml:description.maml:para: Microsoft Graph PowerShell supports two types of authentication: delegated and app-only access. There are a number of cmdlets that can be used to manage the different parameters required during authentication, for example, environment, application ID, and certificate.

Invoke Connect-MgGraph before commands that access Microsoft Graph. This cmdlet obtains access tokens through Azure.Identity and the Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL), or uses a caller-provided access token. Use Get-MgContext to inspect the connected account, tenant, authentication type, and permissions.

On Windows, interactive authentication uses Web Account Manager (WAM) by default. To use browser sign-in instead, run Set-MgGraphOption -DisableLoginByWAM $true before connecting with a custom -ClientId. WAM cannot be disabled for the default Microsoft Graph PowerShell client ID.

command:example.maml:title: Example 1: Delegated access: Using interactive authentication, where you provide the scopes that you require during your session
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "User.Read.All", "Group.ReadWrite.All"

dev:remarks.maml:para: This example shows how to authenticate to graph with scopes.

command:example.maml:title: ----- Example 2: Delegated access: Using device code flow -----
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "User.Read.All", "Group.ReadWrite.All" -UseDeviceAuthentication

dev:remarks.maml:para: This example shows how to authenticate to graph with scopes and device.

command:example.maml:title: Example 3: Using your own access token
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> $SecureAccessToken = ConvertTo-SecureString -String $AccessToken -AsPlainText -Force PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -AccessToken $SecureAccessToken

dev:remarks.maml:para: This example converts a plain-text Microsoft Graph token in $AccessToken to the SecureString required by Connect-MgGraph. The token can represent delegated or app-only access. You are responsible for acquiring a replacement when it expires.

command:example.maml:title: Example 4: Delegated access: custom application for Microsoft Graph PowerShell
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -ClientId "YOUR_NEW_APP_ID" -TenantId "YOUR_TENANT_ID"

dev:remarks.maml:para: Follow this link (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/microsoftgraph/authentication-commands?view=graph-powershell-1.0#using-connect-mggraph)for more information on the steps for creating custom applications.

command:example.maml:title: Example 5: App-only access: Using client credential with a certificate - Certificate Thumbprint
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -ClientId "YOUR_APP_ID" -TenantId "YOUR_TENANT_ID" -CertificateThumbprint "YOUR_CERT_THUMBPRINT"

dev:remarks.maml:para: Follow this link (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/microsoftgraph/authentication-commands?view=graph-powershell-1.0#using-connect-mggraph)for more information on how to load the certificate.

command:example.maml:title: Example 6: App-only access: Using client credential with a certificate - Certificate name
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -ClientId "YOUR_APP_ID" -TenantId "YOUR_TENANT_ID" -CertificateName "YOUR_CERT_SUBJECT"

dev:remarks.maml:para: Follow this link (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/microsoftgraph/authentication-commands?view=graph-powershell-1.0#using-connect-mggraph)for more information on how to load the certificate.

command:example.maml:title: Example 7: App-only access: Using client credential with a certificate - Certificate
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> $Cert = Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My\$CertThumbprint PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -ClientId "YOUR_APP_ID" -TenantId "YOUR_TENANT_ID" -Certificate $Cert

dev:remarks.maml:para: Follow this link (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/microsoftgraph/authentication-commands?view=graph-powershell-1.0#using-connect-mggraph)for more information on how to load the certificate.

command:example.maml:title: ---------- Example 8: Using client secret credentials ----------
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> $ClientSecretCredential = Get-Credential -Credential "Client_Id" # Enter client_secret in the password prompt. PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -TenantId "Tenant_Id" -ClientSecretCredential $ClientSecretCredential

dev:remarks.maml:para: This authentication method is ideal for background interactions. It does not require a user to physically sign in.

command:example.maml:title: Example 9: Using managed identity: System-assigned managed identity
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -Identity

dev:remarks.maml:para: Uses an automatically managed identity on a service instance. The identity is tied to the lifecycle of a service instance.

command:example.maml:title: Example 10: Using managed identity: User-assigned managed identity
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -Identity -ClientId "User_Assigned_Managed_identity_Client_Id"

dev:remarks.maml:para: Uses a user created managed identity as a standalone Azure resource.

command:example.maml:title: ------ Example 11: Connecting to an environment or cloud ------
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Get-MgEnvironment Name AzureADEndpoint GraphEndpoint Type ---- --------------- ------------- ---- BleuCloud https://login.sovcloud-identity.fr https://graph.svc.sovcloud.fr Built-in China https://login.chinacloudapi.cn https://microsoftgraph.chinacloudapi.cn Built-in DelosCloud https://login.sovcloud-identity.de https://graph.svc.sovcloud.de Built-in Global https://login.microsoftonline.com https://graph.microsoft.com Built-in GovSGCloud https://login.sovcloud-identity.sg https://graph.svc.sovcloud.sg Built-in USGov https://login.microsoftonline.us https://graph.microsoft.us Built-in USGovDoD https://login.microsoftonline.us https://dod-graph.microsoft.us Built-in PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -Environment USGov

dev:remarks.maml:para: When you use Connect-MgGraph, you can choose to target other environments. By default, Connect-MgGraph targets the global public cloud.

command:example.maml:title: Example 12: Connecting to a sovereign cloud with a custom application
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -ClientId "YOUR_APP_CLIENT_ID" -TenantId "YOUR_TENANT_ID" -Environment BleuCloud -Scopes "User.Read.All"

dev:remarks.maml:para: Sovereign cloud environments (BleuCloud, DelosCloud, GovSGCloud) require a custom application registration. You cannot use the default Microsoft Graph PowerShell application in these environments. When registering your application, add an additional redirect URI of `ms-appx-web://Microsoft.AAD.BrokerPlugin/<YOUR_APP_CLIENT_ID>` to support WAM broker-based authentication. Requires Microsoft.Graph.Authentication v2.36.1 or later.

command:example.maml:title: Example 13: Connecting to a sovereign cloud when WAM authentication hangs
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Set-MgGraphOption -DisableLoginByWAM $true PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -ClientId "YOUR_APP_CLIENT_ID" -TenantId "YOUR_TENANT_ID" -Environment BleuCloud

dev:remarks.maml:para: If the authentication popup hangs or times out when connecting to a sovereign cloud (for example, from a jumpbox), WAM broker-based login may not work in that environment. Disable WAM to use interactive browser sign-in instead. You only need to run `Set-MgGraphOption -DisableLoginByWAM $true` once; the setting persists across sessions.

command:example.maml:title: Example 14: Limiting token caching to the current process
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -ContextScope Process

dev:remarks.maml:para: Use -ContextScope Process to keep tokens in memory for the current PowerShell process instead of persisting them across sessions. This controls token persistence, not account selection; it does not force a different identity or disable Windows single sign-on.

command:example.maml:title: Example 15: Delegated access: Pre-populating the account during interactive sign-in
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "User.Read.All" -LoginHint "user@contoso.com"

dev:remarks.maml:para: Use -LoginHint to pre-populate the account during interactive browser or WAM sign-in. A matching cached authentication record can be reused for that account, but an account picker, consent, or other authentication prompt may still be required. This parameter does not guarantee silent sign-in and is not used with -UseDeviceCode.

maml:description.maml:para: Once you're signed in, you'll remain signed in until you invoke Disconnect-MgGraph. Microsoft Graph PowerShell automatically refreshes the access token for you and sign-in persists across PowerShell sessions because Microsoft Graph PowerShell securely caches the token.

Use Disconnect-MgGraph to sign out. This clears the persisted MSAL token cache from disk when using CurrentUser context scope, as well as removing the in-memory token cache and authentication record. Use the -SignOutFromBroker switch to additionally remove cached accounts from the Windows broker (WAM); note that the broker store is shared at the OS level, so this can also sign you out of other broker-enabled applications (for example Visual Studio, Azure CLI, or Azure PowerShell) that use the same Windows account.
Determines how PowerShell responds to progress updates generated by this cmdlet. This is a common parameter introduced in PowerShell 7.4.

Also removes cached accounts from the Windows broker (WAM). This is a shared, OS-level store, so it may sign you out of other broker-enabled applications (e.g. Visual Studio, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell) using the same Windows account.
Determines how PowerShell responds to progress updates generated by this cmdlet. This is a common parameter introduced in PowerShell 7.4.

Also removes cached accounts from the Windows broker (WAM). This is a shared, OS-level store, so it may sign you out of other broker-enabled applications (e.g. Visual Studio, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell) using the same Windows account.

command:example.maml:title: ------------- Example 1: Using Disconnect-MgGraph -------------
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Disconnect-MgGraph

dev:remarks.maml:para: Use Disconnect-MgGraph to sign out.

command:example.maml:title: Example 2: Sign out and also clear the Windows broker (WAM) cache
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Disconnect-MgGraph -SignOutFromBroker

dev:remarks.maml:para: Signs out and additionally removes cached accounts from the Windows broker (WAM). Because the broker store is shared at the OS level, this can also sign you out of other broker-enabled applications (for example Visual Studio, Azure CLI, or Azure PowerShell) using the same Windows account.

command:example.maml:title: -------- Example 1: Disable web account manager support --------
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Set-MgGraphOption -DisableLoginByWAM $True

dev:remarks.maml:para: Disables sign in via Web Account Manager (WAM). Note: This only takes effect when using a custom ClientId. When using the default ClientId, WAM remains enabled regardless of this setting.

command:example.maml:title: --- Example 2: Disable WAM for sovereign cloud environments ---
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Set-MgGraphOption -DisableLoginByWAM $true PS C:\> Connect-MgGraph -ClientId "YOUR_APP_CLIENT_ID" -TenantId "YOUR_TENANT_ID" -Environment BleuCloud

dev:remarks.maml:para: If WAM broker-based authentication hangs or times out when connecting to a sovereign cloud environment (such as BleuCloud, DelosCloud, or GovSGCloud), disable WAM to fall back to interactive browser sign-in. This can occur when authenticating from environments like jumpboxes. The setting persists across PowerShell sessions.

command:example.maml:title: -------- Example 1: Set Http client timeout in seconds --------
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Set-MgRequestContext -ClientTimeout 5 ClientTimeout RetryDelay MaxRetry RetriesTimeLimit ------------- ---------- -------- ---------------- 00:00:05 3 2 00:00:00

dev:remarks.maml:para: Sets Http client timeout in seconds.

command:example.maml:title: Example 2: Set the maximum time in seconds allowed for request retries
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Set-MgRequestContext -RetriesTimeLimit 2 ClientTimeout RetryDelay MaxRetry RetriesTimeLimit ------------- ---------- -------- ---------------- 00:00:05 3 2 00:00:02

dev:remarks.maml:para: Sets the maximum time in seconds allowed for request retries.

command:example.maml:title: -- Example 3: Set the maximum number of retries for a request --
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Set-MgRequestContext -MaxRetry 2 ClientTimeout RetryDelay MaxRetry RetriesTimeLimit ------------- ---------- -------- ---------------- 00:00:05 3 2 00:00:02

dev:remarks.maml:para: Sets the maximum number of retries for a request.

command:example.maml:title: Example 4: Set the waiting time in seconds before retrying a request
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Set-MgRequestContext -RetryDelay 3 ClientTimeout RetryDelay MaxRetry RetriesTimeLimit ------------- ---------- -------- ---------------- 00:00:05 3 2 00:00:02

dev:remarks.maml:para: Sets the waiting time in seconds before retrying a request.
